messages:
lucy: heads up — we're seeing a ~25% p95 latency regression on serving-runtime in prod us-west1 starting ~09:00. collected nsys traces, looks correlated with the canary kernel change.

omar: which route and model/version?

lucy: route: /v1/generate (redwood-7b), pinned v2. The new fused_matmul kernel landed in canary yesterday.

ben: can you paste a tiny nsys timeline slice or top-of-trace summary?

lucy: paste from the nsys top-level timeline:
```
# nsys excerpt (summarized)
GPU queue time:  70% of wall time (long queue stacks)
matmul_fused_kernel (single launch): compute bursts ~30%
KV cache lookup ops: spike at 0.34s with 4x miss rate vs baseline
ContinuousBatch window: median expanded from ~12ms -> ~48ms
driver launch prep (host): multiple 10-50ms spikes
```

maria: pattern = launch overhead + longer kernel cold start -> brokered requests pile up -> continuous batching stretches window. kv cache TTLs worsen misses during longer windows.

omar: do we see host-side stalls (ioctl / memcpy prep) in perfetto?

lucy: yes — perfetto slice shows repeated nvml/ioctl and H2D prep work:
```text
SYSCALL ioctl(nvml): 120ms aggregate between kernel launches
memcpy H2D prep: 40ms spikes correlated with first launch in batch
```

ben: hypothesis: fused_matmul reduces per-token compute but has higher per-launch fixed cost. When traffic is bursty, the runtime's continuous-batching heuristic grows the window to amortize throughput, but the larger window increases kv-cache churn and queue time. Net effect: higher p95.

maria: makes sense. Possible mitigations: 1) temporary affinity rule to prefer the old matmul for small batch counts; 2) pre-warm/persistent launch for fused kernel; 3) cap continuous-batching window for this model family.

lucy: quick test: I'll rollback kernel on one canary host and re-run the same workload.

sre-bot: deploy rollback started — rollout id r-8842 to canary-host-3 :rocket:

lucy: rolled back on canary-host-3, re-collected nsys slice (will share).

(10m later)

lucy: post-rollback quick numbers: p95 returned to baseline; nsys now shows queue time down to ~18% and compute up to ~82% (opposite of the regressed trace). KV cache miss spike gone.

omar: that strongly indicates the new kernel's launch characteristics are the root cause.

ben: proposal for next steps:
- revert fused_matmul in stable until we ship warmup + batching cap
- implement a 'kernel-affinity' threshold: prefer legacy matmul when predicted batch <= 8
- add persistent kernel resident option (lazy prelaunch) for fused kernels
- telemetry alert: batch-window drift >2x baseline triggers perf regression alarm

maria: I'll draft the RFC with perf graphs and suggested config knobs. assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml for joint work.

ben: RFC created: https://r.infra/p/rfcs/1267 (links traces + nsys diff)

lucy: tagging @omar @ben @maria. uploading full traces to bucket rdx-nsys/1995006789.zip — sharing ACL with eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

omar: thanks — once we have warmup + cap, we should A/B the fused kernel behind a flag and monitor p50/p95 and kv-cache hit rate.

maria: noted. I'll add detailed ev-covered perf tests to the canary harness so the telemetry can catch this earlier.

lucy: great. closing the immediate firefight. follow-ups in RFC + ticket.
